key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics plus ferroelectric materials could enable self-powered edge AI by jointly supplying harvested energy, storage, and low-power in-memory computation.
engineering_relevance: The paper frames a practical pathway for distributed intelligence hardware that reduces data-transfer energy and dependence on centralized data centers.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for reliable edge-device energy harvesting.
Compare emerging materials against the power, storage, and compute needs of distributed intelligence.
Argue that (anti)ferroelectrics can help with both electrostatic energy storage and neuromorphic in-memory operation.
evidence_signal: This is a perspective article, so the evidence is a requirements analysis and materials comparison rather than a new experimental dataset.
watch_item: The concept depends on simultaneously meeting energy-harvesting, storage, and device-integration targets, which remains a materials and systems-integration challenge.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
